{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.4 (TrueLink Hosting, Licence and Support Agreement)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review — verified findings, redline positions and walk-away items

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and recorded 18 findings: **6 deviations**, **2 missing clauses** and **10 compliant** positions. The commercial architecture is generally favourable to us on the sourcing and exit side — there is no exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicit, MFN or liquidated-damages obligation on Client; Client holds a unilateral termination-for-convenience right under § 14; the § 13 term is one year with a mutual 30-day non-renewal window; and TrueLink has granted us a rate MFN and a first-year price freeze. TrueLink also has no audit right over our records or systems.

The risk is concentrated in three places. First, **liability is one-sided**: the only limitation caps TrueLink at 12 months' hosting/support fees while Client's very broad § 12(a) indemnity is entirely uncapped — this is expressly in playbook walk-away territory. Second, there is **no vendor IP indemnity and no performance warranty**: TrueLink's only express warranty is Year 2000 date processing, its standard of care is self-referential, and its indemnity covers only its own breach, so third-party infringement claims on the Interface and hosted services sit with us. Third, **our data and paid-for work product have no ownership anchor**: § 2(d) confirms TrueLink's rights in the Interface, nothing confirms Client's rights in Client Content, Client IP or the Support Services results, and § 8(d) grants TrueLink a broad licence to exploit Credit Data. Two further gaps compound the hosting exposure: **no post-termination transition or data-return mechanic** and **no insurance obligation** on a vendor that processes consumer credit data. Assignment (§ 15) also blocks our own M&A without a successor carve-out or reasonableness standard.

Our redlines are minimal and additive: we have inserted the missing vendor-side protections rather than reopening the commercial bargain (for example, we left § 12(a) as drafted and expressly preserved the § 8(d) Credit Data licence).

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability (cap, mutuality, carve-outs) | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE. |
| 6 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE. |
| 7 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE. |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| 10 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT |
| 11 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| 12 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE. |
| 13 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant (at fallback) | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| 14 | Medium | MFN — MFN burdening Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. |
| 15 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant (at fallback) | § 5 COMPENSATION. |
| 16 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT |
| 17 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 12 INDEMNITY. |

### Deviations and gaps — what we changed and why

**1. Vendor indemnity (critical, § 12 INDEMNITY.).** § 12(b) limits TrueLink's indemnity to claims arising out of its own breach or failure to perform. There is no indemnity for third-party allegations that the Interface or hosted services infringe IP rights, and no non-infringement warranty elsewhere — the only infringement covenants run in TrueLink's favour or against Client at §§ 2 and 8(e). That fails even the fallback, which requires a vendor IP indemnity, while Client's § 12(a) indemnity is broad (Client breach, Web Site/Client Content, and injury or damage from anything transmitted from the Web Site). *Redline:* new § 12(c) at the preferred position — IP infringement, breach of law, TrueLink-caused unauthorised access to Client Content/Credit Data, and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with standard notice/control/cooperation procedure and Client Content and Client-modification carve-outs. We left § 12(a) as drafted to keep the edit minimal.

**2. Ownership of data and work product (critical, § 2 LICENSE.).** The only ownership provision, § 2(d), confirms TrueLink's rights in the Interface and says nothing about our side of the line. There is no affirmative statement that Client retains all right, title and interest in Client Content, Client IP or the borrower/loan data transmitted through the Interface (Client Content ownership is acknowledged only on discontinuation of hosting, in § 13), and no ownership or licence provision for the results of the Support Services we pay for — §§ 10(b) and 10(c) treat those results only as confidential/Client Proprietary Information, which is not ownership. Combined with the § 8(d) worldwide licence to "use, distribute, disseminate, license, resell, exploit" Credit Data, our data and paid-for work product have no ownership anchor, failing the fallback (at minimum a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to deliverables). *Redline:* minimal ownership clause — Client retains all rights in its content, IP and data (expressly preserving the existing § 8(d) Credit Data bargain), Support Services results assigned to Client with a licence back for embedded TrueLink IP, TrueLink's Interface ownership preserved, no joint ownership.

**3. Limitation of liability (critical, § 12 INDEMNITY.).** The only limitation (buried in the indemnity section) caps TrueLink at 12 months' hosting/support compensation while Client's liability, including under the broad § 12(a) indemnity, is entirely uncapped. There is no defined carve-out set (only TrueLink's own gross negligence/wilful misconduct is excepted) and no confirmation that Client's payment obligations sit outside the cap. *Redline:* mutual, agreement-wide cap at the greater of 12 months' fees and US$1,000,000, plus a single Excluded Claims sentence (indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct). We have **not** added a mutual consequential-damages waiver — its absence preserves our recovery against the vendor, so we note rather than redline it.

**4. Assignment (high, § 12 INDEMNITY.).** § 15 is the only assignment provision. No change-of-control language appears anywhere, so TrueLink has no CoC termination or re-pricing right (that limb is satisfied). However, consent is required with no reasonableness standard and no carve-out for a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets — only a "financially responsible affiliate" carve-out — which fails the fallback on both material terms and lets TrueLink block our M&A or reorganisation. *Redline:* Client successor carve-out on notice, consent not unreasonably withheld, bar on TrueLink assigning to a competitor of ours, and confirmation that a change of control of Client is not an assignment and triggers no TrueLink right. Mutual structure otherwise preserved.

**5. Licence scope (high, § 2 LICENSE.).** The grant runs to "Client" only; Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf are not licensed, and the only expansion mechanic (amending Exhibit "A" sites on notice under § 2(b)(ii)) covers locations, not entities — failing the fallback ("Affiliates covered on written notice"). Transfer is likewise blocked by § 15. *Redline:* extend the grant to Affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf (Client responsible for their compliance) and add a mutual successor-transfer carve-out. Positively, the licence is not revocable at TrueLink's discretion, so this is not walk-away territory. Noted but not flagged: § 13's automatic cut-off of §§ 2 and 3 for breach of §§ 8a–8c has no cure period, and the licence is not perpetual/paid-up.

**10. Performance warranty (medium, § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT).** TrueLink's only express warranty (§ 9) is Year 2000 date processing. There is no conformance-to-documentation, malicious-code or compliance-with-laws warranty and no repair/replace/refund or re-performance remedy; § 11's standard of care requires only the care TrueLink "customarily exercised by it for its own operations" — self-referential, not industry standard, and with no warranty remedy. The disclaimer is qualified by "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT," so no carve-out is needed; the problem is that there is no express warranty to preserve. This fails even the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies). *Redline:* preferred 12-month conformance warranty, professional and workmanlike services, no malicious code, compliance with laws, repair/replace/refund at TrueLink's option, with 90 days flagged as an acceptable fallback.

**11. Transition assistance and data return (medium, missing, § 12 INDEMNITY.).** This is a hosting agreement in which TrueLink holds Client Content and Credit Data, yet there is no exit provision. § 13 only confirms Client's ownership of its domains and Client Content and makes Client responsible for arranging a new name server/hosting environment within 30/60 days; § 14 merely continues services to the end of the month following notice. Neither obliges TrueLink to provide transition assistance, to return or export our data in usable format, or to delete and certify deletion; § 10 has no return-of-materials mechanic. Short of the fallback (90 days' assistance plus export within 30 days). *Redline:* insert the preferred transition/data-return and certified-deletion paragraph into § 14, noting the 90-day fallback in the comment.

**18. Vendor insurance (low, missing, § 12 INDEMNITY.).** "Insurance" does not appear in the document, and review of §§ 13–30 and the covenants and indemnity sections confirms no insurance obligation on TrueLink, which hosts our Web Site and processes consumer credit data. Both the fallback (E&O US$1M / cyber US$2M) and the preferred position are unmet. *Redline:* new § 31 after § 30 — CGL US$1M/2M, E&O US$2M, cyber US$5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request, with fallback limits offered in the comment.

### Compliant positions worth preserving

- **No exclusivity or non-compete on Client** — § 2(a) is non-exclusive and expressly confirms Client "is not obligated to utilize the License and is free to acquire, develop, license or otherwise utilize any other hardware, software system," and the referenced Non-Competition Agreement limits TrueLink, not us. Preferred position; hold this language.
- **No liquidated damages, penalties or early-termination fee**; no MFN and no non-solicit burdening Client; TrueLink's § 6 rate MFN and first-year price freeze run in our favour.
- **No TrueLink audit right** over our usage, records or systems — better than preferred. We should not introduce audit language; if the vendor adds it, hold to once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, vendor cost. § 8(f) technical mechanisms operate inside TrueLink's own hosted environment and are not an audit.
- **Termination for convenience** — § 14 gives Client a unilateral exit (roughly 30–60 days' effective notice) with no termination charge; TrueLink has no mid-term convenience right and the term is 12 months, not multi-year. Minor points noted only: no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees (moot, as § 5 bills monthly in arrears) and TrueLink's 30-day (not 90-day) non-renewal notice, which we hold reciprocally.
- **Renewal** — § 13: one-year initial term, successive one-year renewals, mutual 30-day non-renewal window. No vendor renewal reminder and no CPI/3% uplift cap; § 6 freezes hosting costs for year one and adds the rate MFN, so no clear unilateral uplift right. Take the reminder and uplift cap opportunistically only if the term is reopened.
- **Governing law** — §§ 26–27 select California law and exclusive California (San Luis Obispo County) courts; no arbitration, no foreign seat. This sits at the playbook fallback rather than the preferred New York position, so we accept it. Noted only: venue is the licensor's local county rather than a neutral California forum, and § 28 imports Civil Code § 1717 fee-shifting.
- **Minimum commitments** — the § 5(a) monthly fee floor sits at our fallback: bounded by the one-year auto-renewing term, subject to the § 14 at-will exit (approximately 30 days), with no shortfall penalty, acceleration or take-or-pay, and § 2(a) confirming no obligation to use the licence. Accepted without redline.

---

## 3. Walk-away items

1. **Uncapped Client liability against a capped vendor (LOL-CAP, § 12 INDEMNITY.).** Squarely within the playbook walk-away scenario — "Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped." A mutual, agreement-wide cap with the standard uncapped carve-outs is a condition of signature.
2. **No insurance from a vendor processing personal data (INSURANCE, § 12 INDEMNITY.).** TrueLink hosts our Web Site and processes consumer credit data with no insurance obligation, triggering the rule's walk-away scenario. We require at least the fallback limits (E&O US$1M / cyber US$2M).

For completeness, three walk-away triggers were tested and are **not** engaged: the licence is not revocable at TrueLink's discretion (LICENSE); there is no multi-year term without a Client convenience right (T4C) and no multi-year take-or-pay or usage cap (MINCOMMIT); and there is no audit right against us (AUDIT).

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the six deviations and two gaps: mutual liability cap with Excluded Claims; new § 12(c) vendor indemnity; Client ownership clause; § 15 successor/reasonableness/no-competitor amendments; licence extension to Affiliates and contractors; § 9 performance warranty; § 14 transition assistance, data return and certified deletion; and new § 31 insurance. All comments carry the `[Playbook]` prefix and state the fallback where one exists.
2. **Prioritise for negotiation** in this order: liability mutuality, vendor IP indemnity, data and work-product ownership. These three are critical and interlock — the cap is only meaningful once there is an indemnity and warranty to draw on.
3. **Diligence the separate Non-Competition Agreement** referenced at § 8(d). It is not attached; confirm it contains no reciprocal restriction on Client and no personnel restrictions.
4. **Complete the commercial blanks** before execution: the minimum monthly amounts in § 5(a) and the programmer commitment period in § 4. Note that § 6 carves the minimum monthly fees out of Client's documentation and dispute rights — we should ask for that carve-out to be removed as a billing-transparency point. If the § 4 blank is completed with a long period, clarify that it does not hold the Support Services minimum open past a § 14 termination.
5. **Hold the favourable terms** identified above (no exclusivity, no non-compete, no audit, no MFN or LD on Client, Client convenience right, vendor rate MFN) and resist any reciprocity trade that would introduce an audit right, a consequential-damages waiver or an exclusivity/minimum-volume obligation on us.

*Findings in this memo reflect the verified review record only; verification status on each finding is "skipped" and no conclusions have been drawn beyond the sections cited above.*"}
